1. Following [Recitation 1](../recitations/recitation-1.qmd), load the [CPS-ASEC data](https://github.com/josephmullins/ECON4538/tree/main/data) and perform the same steps to deflate nominal \$ values to 2017 dollars. Remember that ASEC income variables refer to the previous calendar year, so deflate using the price index of the income year (`INCYEAR = YEAR - 1`) and label your plots by income year.
2. In @Heathcote2023, the *Household Pooling index* $HP_{t}$ is defined as
$$ HP_{t} = \frac{var(y_{it}) - var(\bar{y}_{it})}{var(y_{it})}$$
where $y_{it}$ is the income of individual $i$ in year $t$ and $\bar{y}_{it}$ is per-person income of the household that individual $i$ lives in. Both variances are taken across individuals (so each individual is assigned their household's per-person income), weighted by the person weight `ASECWT`. Calculate this index when $y$ is defined solely as labor market earnings (i.e. wage earnings) and when $y$ is defined as labor market + business income. Plot both lines to compare them and comment on any differences.
3. Calculate and plot an equivalent index for government transfers where now $y_{it}$ is per-person household earnings (business + wage income) and $\bar{y}_{it}$ is per-person household earnings + government transfers. As in question 2, compute the variances across individuals using `ASECWT`. You can follow the variable for transfers we constructed in Recitation 1. Name at least one way that this measure differs from the measure used to construct the Government redistribution index in Figure 19 of @Heathcote2023.
4. Re-compute the index from question 3 for individuals in the poorest households: those whose per-person household *earnings* (wage + business income, before transfers) are below the 20th percentile in each year. Compute the 20th percentile across individuals using `ASECWT`, as in question 3. Comment on any differences with the previous figure.
5. In Recitation 1, we plotted the share of total transfers coming from each of five programs. Re-calculate this share for only the poorest 20% of households (as measured by per-person household earnings, using the household weight `ASECWTH` as in Recitation 1) and comment on any differences you see compared to the original figure (**extra credit**)
